Aurora text conformance

Incomplete: exact Windows-native parity still fails.

C remains the shared default. These changes are in the opt-in native-refined renderer and remain pure D. Improved averages, nonblank output and passing application tests do not establish glyph quality.

The tests compare the same glyph IDs at the same positions against this Windows machine’s native grayscale output. The scopes below overlap. Every unequal pixel is a failure; clipped captures also fail.

What changed

Diagonal hints now use the moved line for projection and retain a separate original vector. Natural diagonal rounding and cut-in use the appropriate extra resolution. Relative axis distances and IUP interpolation preserve original-point ratios, including Windows’ signed IUP rounding and rounded interval guards. Curve-changing instructions survive into scan conversion. Quadratic intersections remain stable at horizontal extrema.

The 1px refinement skips glyph instructions while retaining the initial scaled coordinates; the nine-font 846-glyph check is unchanged. Native generated-font probes expose this behavior, and still retain unresolved tiny-outline cases.

Remaining gaps: native dropout controls still do not reach Aurora’s scan converter; Times and Courier can lose thin strokes. Composite child hint programs are not executed. Legacy gasp behavior and additional outline/coverage differences remain. This is a rasterization test, not a certification of shaping, fallback or every platform.
